mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing liquidity, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates robust demand recovery, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both HOUST and RSAFS rising) fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession supply recovery phase, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals expanding manufacturing output and improving corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising in a post-recession context.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing consumer spending (RSAFS) is a direct driver of near-term S&P 500 gains, with positive returns observed over the next 5 trading days in the majority of cases.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, the Federal Reserve typically initiates monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in unemployment and rise in employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strong labor market, which consistently generates positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE falling and PAYEMS rising) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), higher interest rates reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%.
